statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: New Zealand Companies Office (www.business.govt.nz / www.companiesoffice.govt.nz) – 'Check company names' online name reservation and incorporation portal
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Names may be registered in English script only; deaths of Maori and other non-English script are transliterated phonetically into romanized Latin characters; all official corporate names must be represented in English letters and must comply with the Companies Act 1993 prohibited-name provisions.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Companies Office rejects a proposed name, the applicant may file a formal written objection or request for reconsideration via the Companies Office website or by email to the Companies Office Registrar; the applicant must cite the name reservation reference, include supporting evidence of lawfulness and non-conflict, and request an administrative review under section 22 of the Companies Act 1993; a rejected name may be re-filed in a different format or with additional distinguishing wording; judicial review of an adverse determination is available in the High Court of New Zealand.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A registered office must be a physical address in New Zealand. However, a virtual office service can be used as the registered office if it provides a physical street address where documents can be served. For ISIC 6201 (software development) and medical EMR SaaS, a virtual office is generally acceptable for incorporation and initial registration, but the company must maintain a practical physical presence or contractual data-local processing arrangements only to the extent required by New Zealand data-residency obligations under the Health Information Privacy Code 2020. Full commercial substance will be assessed by enforcement authorities; a purely non-resident managed company is legal but may be subject to scrutiny for GST/tax residence and anti-avoidance rules.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low (estimated unannounced on-site inspection probability: 3-7% per year; inspection likelihood increases only upon AML/CFT or consumer protection complaints, or if the registered address is shared with high-risk shell-company clusters).

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 1993 (Public Act 1993 No 105) – ss. 12 (formation of company), 13 (manner of incorporation), 14 (certificate of incorporation), 15–23 (registered name), 32–33 (allotment of shares), 124–125 (registered office), 126 (address for service), 151–154 (director eligibility and consent), 189 (board powers), 218–222 (shareholder communication and registers); Companies (Fees) Regulations 2019; Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013 ss. 34–37 (exempt securities offers); Contract and Commercial Law Act 2017 (electronically executed documents).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: New Zealand Companies Office – an operating arm of the Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE), administered by the Registrar of Companies
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Companies Office Form 1 – 'Application for Incorporation of a Company' (lodged electronically through the New Zealand Companies Register portal), accompanied by Form 2 'Notice of Registered Office' and Form 3 'Consent to Acting as Director' where applicable
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital under the Companies Act 1993. The International Company (CK_IC) may be incorporated with a single ordinary share of NZD 1.00 (or any denomination determined by the board) paid partly or fully in cash or in kind. No escrow account, capital deposit, or currency importation declaration is required in New Zealand for non-resident share subscription; 100% non-resident ownership is permitted without exchange control approval.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF [COMPANY NAME] LIMITED (the 'Company'): RESOLVED, by unanimous written resolution of all directors of the Company on [DATE]:
(1) CONSTITUTION — that the Constitution of the Company, as filed with the New Zealand Companies Register on [DATE], be and is hereby adopted as the supreme governing instrument of the Company.
(2) SHARE SUBSCRIPTION — that the allotment of [1,000] ordinary shares of NZD 0.01 each, being a total issued consideration of NZD 10.00, be and is hereby authorised, issued and allotted to [OVERSEAS PARENT COMPANY], and that the directors are authorised to compile the share register and issue Share Certificate(s) numbered CS-001 accordingly.
(3) REGISTERED OFFICE — that the registered office of the Company be fixed at [STREET ADDRESS, CITY, NEW ZEALAND] and that the Company Secretary is authorised to file Form 2 Notice of Registered Office with the New Zealand Companies Office.
(4) OFFICER APPOINTMENTS — that [NAME] be and is hereby appointed Managing Director, [NAME] be and is hereby appointed Company Secretary, and [NAME] be and is hereby appointed Chief Financial Officer, each to serve until removal or resignation under the Companies Act 1993.
(5) BANKING — that the Company open an operating account at a New Zealand registered trading bank and authorise signatories as separately resolved.
(6) TAX OBJECTS — that the Company apply to the Inland Revenue Department for an IRD number, GST registration and employer registration (where applicable), and that the directors take all steps necessary to achieve tax compliance from the effective date of incorporation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Register online portal (Registrar of Companies, MBIE)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct an electronic name availability search against the Companies Register database and reserve the proposed name '[COMPANY NAME] LIMITED' for a renewable statutory period. The name must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered name or reserved name and must not contravene Section 22 of the Companies Act 1993 (false, misleading, or offensive names, or restricted words requiring consent). File the electronic name reservation application, certify compliance with s.22, and obtain the reservation number for use in the incorporation application.
required_dossiers: Certification of name compliance under s.22
Consent of sector regulator for restricted words (e.g., 'Medical' or 'Clinic') if required
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar rejects the proposed name, file a fresh name reservation with a distinguishable alternative, or submit a written application under s.24 requesting the Registrar's consent to use the otherwise restricted name, attaching supporting evidence of lawful entitlement.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Completion and Execution of Constitutional Documents and Director Consents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Founding directors and incorporating attorney (barrister and solicitor of the High Court of New Zealand)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare and execute the Company Constitution (or elect to adopt the default Table 1 constitution under ss. 28–29). Every proposed director must complete and sign Form 3 'Consent to Acting as Director' confirming qualification under s.151, and must provide a New Zealand address for service under s.126. The incorporator must also resolve the initial share capital, class rights, director borrowing powers, company name, and registered office address. All signatures on the constitution may be executed electronically pursuant to the Contract and Commercial Law Act 2017.
required_dossiers: Form 3 Consent to Acting as Director for each proposed director
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct any defective consent or declaration by having the director re-execute the document; if disqualification is discovered, replace the director and file amended consents before submission of the incorporation application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Lodgment of Form 1 Incorporation Application
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office via the Companies Register portal (www.companiesoffice.govt.nz)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in to the Companies Register using RealMe authentication, select 'Incorporate a Company', and complete Form 1. Enter the proposed name, registered office address, address for service, shareholder particulars, director details, and the share structure. Attach the executed Constitution and Form 3 consents as supporting dossiers. Complete the anti-money-laundering customer due diligence verification where a reporting entity (legal adviser or accountant) lodges on behalf of the ultimate beneficial owner. Certify the statutory declarations, pay the incorporation fee of NZD 150 by electronic funds transfer, and submit the application.
required_dossiers: PDF copy of Form 3 for each director
Landlord consent to use registered office address
AML/CFT identification of all ultimate beneficial owners
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar raises a defect notice under s.369, access the pending application queue and amend/rectify the data fields within 15 working days. Should the defect relate to restricted words or address consent, upload supplementary evidence or revise the entity name and resubmit without loss of payment credit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation and New Zealand Business Number (NZBN)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon successful validation and payment confirmation, the Registrar issues the electronic Certificate of Incorporation, which is conclusively evidenced by s.14 of the Companies Act 1993. The company comes into legal existence on the date of the certificate, and its company registration number and NZBN are auto-generated and linked in the Companies Register profile. The certificate and register summary must be downloaded and archived as conclusory proof of incorporation for banking, tax, and contracting purposes.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate is not generated within the SLA, escalate to the Companies Office national contact centre. For any clerical error on the certificate, file a notice of correction under s.369 with supporting statutory declaration; the Registrar will reissue the corrected certificate within 5 working days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Registration Governance Setup, Tax Identification, and Statutory Registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Directors, Company Secretary, and Inland Revenue Department (IRD)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting and minute the pro forma resolutions: approve allotment of shares, adopt the registered office, appoint officers. Issue physical or electronic share certificates and open the mandatory statutory registers (share register, director register, entry for notices of charges). Apply online to IRD for the IRD number (Form IR596), register for GST (Form GST1) if the enterprise voluntarily or compulsorily exceeds NZD 60,000 annual taxable supplies, and register as an employer for PAYE where New Zealand remunerated staff are engaged. File the company's initial annual return confirmation through the Companies Register and, where applicable, seek Health Information Privacy Code compliance acknowledgements.
required_dossiers: Share certificates and share register entries
Annual return confirmation with Companies Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If IRD defers registration pending verification, present the certificate of incorporation and director identification for enhanced due diligence. For company register errors, apply to the Registrar for rectification under ss. 360 and 369, and file the corrected information within 15 working days of discovery.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Health – Manatū Hauora, through the Health Information Standards Organisation (HISO), together with the New Zealand Medicines and Medical Devices Safety Authority (Medsafe) for any module constituting software as a medical device; local territorial authority (District/City Council) for premises conformity; and the Office of the Privacy Commissioner for health information governance compliance.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: HISO 10064:2017 Health Information Governance Clearance (including HISO 10029 Health Information Security Framework conformance); conditional Medsafe 'Software as a Medical Device (SaMD)' conformity assessment under the Medicines Act 1981 and the IMDRF risk classification framework where the EMR module provides diagnostic or clinical decision-support; ISO 13485 / ISO 27001 certification recommended as a supply-chain licence prerequisite for clinical deployment.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Authority (EPA) New Zealand, acting under the Resource Management Act 1991, the Environmental Protection Authority Act 2011, and the Hazardous Substances and New Organisms Act 1996
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category: EXEMPT – Registration not required. ISIC 6201 (computer programming / SaaS platform for EMR) constitutes a purely digital service with no physical manufacturing plant, no discharge of contaminants to air, land or water, and no industrial or trade premises under Schedule 4 of the National Environmental Standards. Office-based software activity is a permitted activity under the relevant District Plan; the hosting data centre is separately consented by the cloud provider.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Zero-process-discharge compliance for the software operation: no trade wastewater, no hazardous waste streams, and negligible VOC emissions. The entity must comply with the National Environmental Standards for Sources of Drinking Water 2007 (non-applicability), the Waste Minimisation Act 2008 for e-waste recycling, the Electricity (Safety) Regulations 2010 for IT equipment, and the Climate Change Response Act 2002 / NZ ETS reporting obligations for purchased electricity where the company exceeds the disclosure threshold.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire and Emergency New Zealand (FENZ) fire safety means-of-escape certificate under the Fire and Emergency New Zealand Act 2017; building occupancy clearance and structural load inspection by the territorial authority under the Building Act 2004 (including Building Warrant of Fitness where the leased premises contain a specified system); workplace risk assessment, ergonomic workstation compliance, and emergency preparedness plan certified under the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015, together with a workplace electrical safety inspection under the Electricity (Safety) Regulations 2010.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department (Te Tari Taake) of New Zealand; secure online portal: myIR (www.ird.govt.nz); company registration infrastructure: New Zealand Companies Office and New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) registry.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1. Incorporate the International Company (IC) at the New Zealand Companies Office to obtain the NZBN and incorporation certificate. 2. Submit Form IR596 to Inland Revenue to obtain a non-resident/offshore company IRD number. 3. If the IC derives gross income subject to NZ withholding (e.g., dividends, interest, royalties) or makes GST-taxable supplies in NZ, register for income tax/GST via myIR (Form IR356 for GST). 4. For offshore suppliers of remote services into New Zealand, complete the Inland Revenue offshore GST registration in myIR once NZ-consumer turnover exceeds NZD 60,000. 5. Appoint a New Zealand tax agent for myIR digital filing and to maintain the entity's compliance record.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Tax_Exempt_Zone: the CK_IC International Company is treated as a non-resident/exempt company for New Zealand income tax purposes so long as its management and control (central management) are outside New Zealand and it derives no New Zealand-source income. New Zealand taxation applies on a territorial basis only, so offshore-sourced EMR/SaaS subscription revenue is outside the New Zealand income tax net; no entity-level income tax, no capital gains tax, and no dividend withholding tax on exempt foreign-sourced income.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: New Zealand does not operate a US-style check-the-box election. Available statutory/elective mechanisms: (i) Look-Through Company (LTC) election under the Income Tax Act 2007 for closely held NZ-resident companies (up to five owners, tax transparency); (ii) GST group registration election under s 55 Goods and Services Tax Act 1985; (iii) hybrid mismatch election/compliance measures under the Taxation (Neutralising Base Erosion and Profit Shifting) Act 2018; (iv) non-resident 'exempt company' status for a company wholly owned by non-residents that carries on no business in NZ and derives no NZ-source income; and (v) voluntary GST registration for non-resident suppliers of remote services.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax (GST) — a VAT-type consumption tax under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NZD 60,000 of taxable supplies in any consecutive 12-month period. Non-resident suppliers of 'remote services' (including cloud SaaS/EMR software) to New Zealand resident consumers are subject to the same NZD 60,000 threshold and must register under the offshore supplier GST regime; voluntary registration is permitted.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: New Zealand has no mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, API tax-stamping, or government digital stamping for invoices. E-invoicing is voluntary and operates over the Peppol network ('NZ e-Invoicing'); since 1 April 2022 all New Zealand central government agencies are required to accept e-invoices. GST returns and payments are filed electronically through the myIR portal or certified accounting/Xero software; no transactional pre-clearance by the Inland Revenue Department is required.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under ss 11 and 11A Goods and Services Tax Act 1985, the 0% export rate applies where: (i) tangible goods are physically exported from New Zealand within 28 days of supply; (ii) services are supplied to a non-resident recipient who is outside New Zealand at the time of supply (this includes B2B offshore SaaS/EMR subscriptions to foreign medical clinics where the services are performed and consumed outside New Zealand); (iii) services relate directly to land or moveable goods situated outside New Zealand; or (iv) the supply is international carriage. Remote digital services supplied to New Zealand resident end consumers are outside zero rating and attract 15% GST under the offshore supplier registration regime.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: New Zealand Customs electronic Cargo Export Declaration (CusMod single-window export entry)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical export
Inward Remittance Certificate (IRC) or bank/foreign-exchange statement evidencing receipt of export proceeds
Evidence of the offshore recipient's non-resident status (overseas tax identification number or business registry extract) for service zero-rating
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The Inland Revenue Department and New Zealand Customs jointly audit export zero-rating claims. Failure to substantiate export, or non-repatriation of export proceeds within the required window, causes the supply to be recharacterised as taxable at 15% GST with use-of-money interest and retrospective refund clawback. Civil shortfall penalties under the Tax Administration Act 1994 apply at 20% (failure to take reasonable care), 40% (abusive tax position), and 100% (tax evasion); fraudulent zero-rating/export refund claims attract criminal prosecution, penalty tax on top of clawback, and disqualification from the New Zealand Customs electronic clearance system.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of New Zealand – Te Pūtea Matua (RBNZ), the sole statutory banking regulator and apex monetary authority, supplemented by the Financial Markets Authority (FMA) for financial-services conduct and the Overseas Investment Office (OIO) for narrow ex-ante screening of sensitive land and significant business assets. The governing framework is the Reserve Bank of New Zealand Act 2021, the Deposit Takers Act 2023, the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013, the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009, and the Companies Act 1993. New Zealand maintains no separate foreign-exchange licensing or exchange-control administration; the RBNZ's regulatory power attaches to monetary policy and the stability of registered banks rather than to the approval of individual cross-border remittances. For the EMR SaaS International Company, no FX permit, no OIO consent, and no RBNZ pre-approval is required for the treasury architecture described herein.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The New Zealand dollar (NZD, ISO-4217) is a free-floating, fully convertible currency. New Zealand has accepted Article VIII obligations of the IMF Articles of Agreement; consequently there are no current-account or capital-account restrictions, no FX prioritisation, no utilisation ratios, and no convertibility queues. SaaS subscription income from US medical clinics, equity injections from non-resident shareholders, shareholder loan repayments, and profit repatriation are all unrestricted as a matter of exchange-control law. Commercial banks are free to set bid/offer spreads, and settlement is carried out through the CLS system for NZD/USD. The only material friction in repatriation is tax-related: statutory non-resident withholding tax (NRWT) at 15% applies to dividends, interest, and royalties paid by a New Zealand payer, though an applicable double tax agreement may reduce that rate, and the IC's tax-exempt classification means no New Zealand source taxable income arises from its treasury operations. Profit remittance to non-resident owners therefore requires no government approval and is limited solely by documentary compliance and board-approved treasury policy.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. New Zealand abolished all mandatory surrender and conversion obligations for export receipts on 10 December 1984. There is no statutory timeline, no minimum conversion ratio, no retention ceiling, and no FX allocation scheme applicable to export proceeds. A medical-clinic EMR SaaS licence sold into the United States is conceptually an export of services under the Balance of Payments framework, but the resulting USD receipts may be held abroad or in a New Zealand foreign-currency account indefinitely, may be converted to NZD at any time, and may be used directly for offshore operational disbursements without RBNZ permission. The only ongoing obligations are record-keeping duties under section 51 of the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 and, if the entity is selected in a Statistics New Zealand/RBNZ statistical survey, the classification of receipts under Balance of Payments item E422 Software/Cloud Export Proceeds.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account and Operational Account (NZD/USD multi-currency treasury package)
Operational Account with segregated Escrow Facility for client-contract deposits
Capital Escrow Account and Operational Account
Operational Account with FXD/NZD dual-currency ledger

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: SUPPLEMENTARY HIGH / PRIMARY LOW. New Zealand does not maintain a distinct electronic-money-institution (EMI) licence class; an offshore digital EMI such as Airwallex or Wise may lawfully operate as a registered money remitter or stored-value facility under the Financial Service Providers (Registration and Dispute Resolution) Act 2008 and the AMLCFT Act 2009, but it is not a New Zealand registered bank for the purposes of the Reserve Bank of New Zealand Act 2021. Consequently, such an EMI cannot lawfully accept call deposits from the public, cannot lend, and provides no protection under the Depositor Compensation Scheme. For this International Company the practical architecture is: (a) a Tier-1 New Zealand bank account as the primary real-money treasury ledger, capital-escrow vessel, and settlement account for clinic counterparties; and (b) a licensed EMI sidecar, integrated with Stripe_Billing and Bank_Transfer rails, for fast multi-currency merchant settlements, contractor sub-accounts, and multi-region payment localisation. The EMI must be independently licensed in its home jurisdiction, maintain robust sanctions/PEP screening, and accept the same enhanced-due-diligence dossier required by the Tier-1 banks before the treasury committee will commit floating balances above USD 50,000.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote onboarding is legally permissible in New Zealand, assisted by video identity verification and the Digital Identity Services Trust Framework Act 2023; however, in practice, all five Tier-1 banks require at least one director and the ultimate beneficial owner of a non-resident International Company to attend a recorded interactive interview (Zoom/MS Teams) before an account is opened. Physical presence is not an absolute statutory mandate, but it becomes operationally unavoidable when the entity is tax-exempt, has no New Zealand employees, and has a fully offshore ownership chain. A documentary-only onboarding is granted rarely and only where: the company appoints a New Zealand-resident registered agent; the apostilled Certificate of Incumbency and constitutional documents are submitted; a notarised source-of-funds declaration is provided for each investor; and the bank receives a professional-intermediary warranty from the offshore corporate service provider. The typical procedure is a single 30-minute video conference followed by a wet-ink or e-signed relationship mandate, with the first transaction held pending a successful source-of-funds verification.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Offshore 'tax-exempt' International Company classification, with no local employees, no physical premises, and no demonstrable operational substance in New Zealand.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apostilled Certificate of Incorporation and Memorandum/Constitutive Charter; certified Register of Directors and Register of Shareholders; confirmation from the New Zealand Companies Office / IRD that the entity is not carrying on business in New Zealand; a formal business-risk-management narrative; signed EMR licence agreements with US medical clinics; AWS/HIPAA cloud infrastructure invoices; and a board resolution ratifying the treasury account mandate.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial owners residing in a jurisdiction under FATF monitoring or perceived as high-risk for cross-border medical data flows.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Chain-complete ownership diagram from the ultimate natural-person beneficiary to the IC; independent sanctions/PEP screening certificate from a recognised screening provider; notarised and apostilled passports plus address-of-entity certification for each material UBO; professional-intermediary warranty letter from the offshore service provider; and three years of personal or corporate bank references evidencing legitimate source of wealth.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Transaction-profile mismatch between declared medical-SaaS operating flows and large inbound equity injections.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed share-subscription or shareholder-loan agreement; board minutes approving the capital call; a 12-month cash-flow forecast showing that USD clinic receivables remain segregated from capital inflows; a treasury policy stating that capital injections enter the Capital Escrow Account only and are never commingled with Stripe settlement funds; and an independent audit, or management-account confirmation, of the prior-year revenue ledger.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: HIPAA/health-data reputational nexus: the AML analyst flags medical-related cross-border flows as elevated compliance risk even where the underlying SaaS software is low-risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed HIPAA Business Associate Agreement with each US clinic counterparty; SOC 2 Type II attestation and ISO 27001 certificate; a privacy-architecture diagram proving that no protected health information (PHI) is routed through the New Zealand treasury entity; New Zealand Privacy Act 2020 compliance addendum; and a third-party data-processing inventory limited to metadata and workflow configuration.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Zero domestic footprint and absence of a New Zealand banking reference, creating difficulty in verifying the entity's operational history.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Letter of reference from the IC's previous foreign financial institution; notarised 12-month bank statements of the parent or lead investor; a reserved appointment of a New Zealand-registered accounting firm as the AML/CTF data guardian; certificate of good standing from the IC's home registry; and a written undertaking to notify the bank of any change in directors, shareholders, or beneficial ownership within 10 business days.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant protocol: (1) execute an unconditional share-subscription agreement or shareholder loan instrument; (2) instruct the remitter's bank to send SWIFT MT103 with beneficiary field 59 containing the exact IC corporate name, field 50K the true investor name, and field 70 annotated 'EQUI – Equity Subscription / Direct Investment Inflow (BOP DI1)'; (3) route the funds exclusively to the dedicated Capital Escrow Account at the Tier-1 New Zealand bank — never commingle with operating revenue; (4) deliver to the bank the subscription schedule, board resolution, constitutive documents, and a source-of-wealth certificate for each investor before the funds are released to the operational ledger; (5) confirm that the transaction does not trigger the Overseas Investment Act 2005, which is inapplicable to SaaS intangibles and intangible-position treasury balances; (6) book the receipt for Balance of Payments statistical purposes as 'Direct Investment – Equity Capital' if the transaction is sampled by Statistics New Zealand/RBNZ; and (7) retain the MT103 confirmation and investor-side KYC pack for at least 10 years under the AMLCFT Act 2009. No exchange-control authorisation, no RBNZ permit, and no OIO consent is required.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Rails hierarchy: (A) SWIFT MT103, with field 71A set to 'OUR', for all material high-value disbursements — AWS/HIPAA cloud-host, clinical-workflow subcontractors, US medical-clinic licensing commissions, and external legal/compliance counsel — accompanied by purpose code 'TRAD' or 'TECH' and invoice-line remittance data; (B) a Commercial Letter of Credit governed by ICC UCP600, supplemented where fully electronic by eUCP 2.1, only for physical hardware procurement such as secure server appliances deployed at clinic sites, with documents against payment; (C) SWIFT ISO 20022 pain.001/pac.008 for low-value NZD disbursements, payroll, and same-day NZD sweeps; and (D) the payment-aggregation layer: Stripe_Billing receives USD card settlements from US clinics on a T+2 basis and settles into the treasury's USD sub-ledger, while Bank_Transfer uses 3-day direct-debit rails for enterprise clinic accounts. The treasury running rule is a 15:00 NZST daily sweep converting all USD above a two-month operating burn buffer into NZD using the dealing bank's FX desk, leaving a pre-agreed USD floor for forward-horizon obligations.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: NZD/USD deliverable FX forwards with tenors of 1 to 24 months, executed under an ISDA 1998 FX/Currency Definitions master agreement; non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are not necessary because the NZD is fully convertible and the deliverable forward market is deep and liquid.
Cross-currency swaps (CCS) to convert USD-denominated SaaS licence inflows into NZD for multi-year operational runway and to lock the equity capital injection at the capital-escrow date.

Vanilla OTC FX options — ATM straddles, collars, and participating forwards — for protection on anticipated large USD receipts from enterprise clinic contracts where a fixed NZD budget is commitment-critical.

FX spot and rolling FX swaps for weekly treasury-profit repatriation and intra-month liquidity rebalancing, executed with the authorised dealing bank and recorded in the bank's trade-ticket audit trail.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return under the International Companies Act 2010-11
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Cook Islands Financial Supervisory Commission
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after each anniversary date of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing may incur a penalty of up to USD 500 per annual return; continued non-filing for two consecutive years may result in administrative strike-off and dissolution of the company.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Licensed Registered Agent Annual Renewal Confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before the annual anniversary date of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to renew the registered-agent engagement may result in termination of the registered office arrangement and compulsory deregistration if no replacement agent is appointed.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory audit threshold applies to a non-resident tax-exempt International Company. Independent audit is mandatory only where the company holds a regulated financial services licence, issues public securities, or is required by court order or by its constitutive documents.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as adopted under the Cook Islands financial services framework; voluntary statutory financial statements may otherwise be prepared under compliant local GAAP.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No public ultimate beneficial owner register is filed annually. The licensed registered agent must obtain annual confirmation of current shareholders, directors, shareholdings, and beneficial-ownership details for the confidential statutory registers and AML/CFT customer due diligence file. Share transfers must be recorded in the register of members and reflected in the next annual confirmation.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book of Members' and Directors' Meetings

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,000 - 15,000 (only if voluntarily required or court-ordered; not otherwise applicable)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% (qualifying Cook Islands International Company in the tax-exempt offshore zone); 28% if the entity is treated as a New Zealand tax resident through central management and control or a New Zealand fixed establishment
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Statutory exemption from income tax for a compliant International Company carrying on activities outside the Cook Islands and New Zealand; 15% refundable Research and Development tax credit available to a New Zealand-resident operating company; imputation credit system for resident shareholders; available tax pooling and provisional tax discounts; no capital gains tax in the standard corporate regime

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: IR4 (Company Income Tax Return) for a New Zealand-resident company or a non-resident company with a fixed establishment, filed electronically through Inland Revenue myIR
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a standard 31 March balance date, the return is due and terminal tax must be paid by 7 July following the end of the income year; approved non-standard balance dates are aligned to the IRD’s deemed balance-date framework; tax-agent extensions may apply. An exempt International Company does not file an IR4 unless it is re-characterised as a New Zealand resident.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: All assessable income, including New Zealand-source EMR software subscription revenue, implementation fees, training fees, and any deemed income from related-party transactions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter zero if the International Company has no New Zealand-source income and no fixed establishment in New Zealand; support with transfer-pricing and residence documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legitimate business deductions under the Income Tax Act 2007, including software development costs, cloud infrastructure expenses, royalties, employee costs, and amortisation of capitalised EMR platform development.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter only deductions attributable to New Zealand activities; allocation must comply with the arm’s length principle and be documented contemporaneously.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Box 1 less Box 2; the New Zealand taxable result before loss offsets.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the entity is tax-exempt, report zero; do not consolidate offshore group results in the IR4.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Carry-forward losses utilised in the current year, subject to the shareholder continuity requirement of 49% or the business continuity test.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident International Company claiming a New Zealand loss offset must prove continuity of ownership and that the loss arose from New Zealand-sourced activity.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net assessable income after applying available loss offsets.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For an exempt International Company, taxable income is nil; any attribution of New Zealand income to the entity will negate the exemption.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculating income tax at 28% on the taxable income of a New Zealand-resident company; no tax is calculated if the company is exempt.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the non-resident carries on business through a fixed establishment in New Zealand, tax is imposed on the New Zealand attributable business profits only.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Credits such as R&D tax credits, foreign tax credits, resident withholding tax credits, and provisional tax paid.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents may not use imputation credits unless they derive New Zealand-source income that is fully imputed; DTA foreign-tax credits must be claimed in the appropriate schedule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax payable after applying the available credits and rebates.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If residual income tax exceeds NZ$5,000, provisional tax liabilities arise for the next income year, even if the entity is predominantly non-resident.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 9 – Imputation credit account and shareholder dividend schedule
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Information on imputation credits attached to dividends, including supplementary dividend payments to qualifying foreign investors.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: An International Company making no New Zealand dividend payments should leave this schedule blank; a deemed New Zealand resident must complete it before repatriating profits.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Director’s or authorised agent’s declaration that the return is true and complete, and that all books and records are available in New Zealand on request.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The commissioner may require the appointment of a New Zealand resident agent before accepting the return; foreign-director signatures should be accompanied by contact details and agent authorisation.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of NZ$250 per return, statutory late-payment penalties of 1% of the unpaid tax from the first day and continuing daily surcharges, use-of-money interest under Part VII of the Tax Administration Act 1994, and civil shortfall penalties of up to 150% for evasion; persistent non-filing may lead to an IRD default assessment and immediate collection action.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: IR6 (Non-resident Company Tax Return) filed through Inland Revenue myIR for a company that is not resident in New Zealand but derives New Zealand-source income
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a standard 31 March balance date, the IR6 is due by 7 July of the following income year; the terminal tax payment is due on the same date unless an approved extension of time applies.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Income from New Zealand, including fees for EMR software supplied to medical clinics if the income is attributable to a New Zealand fixed establishment, or income derived from contracts negotiated and performed in New Zealand.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A Cook Islands International Company should attach a copy of its certificate of incorporation and a statement explaining why it has no New Zealand fixed establishment; if the facts show New Zealand management and control, the IR6 will be rejected and an IR4 required.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Part B – Expenses incurred in deriving New Zealand income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Expenses directly incurred in producing the New Zealand-source income, including royalties paid for licensed EMR software and costs of New Zealand support personnel.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: All cross-border charges to the non-resident company must satisfy transfer-pricing rules; absence of contemporaneous documentation may result in disallowance.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculating the tax liability on the net New Zealand-source income of the non-resident; separately reconciling non-resident withholding tax on dividends, interest, and royalties.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim the applicable double-taxation agreement rate only after submitting a valid Tax Residency Certificate; otherwise the statutory NRWT rate applies.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Certification by the company and its New Zealand agent.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Failure to appoint a New Zealand agent may lead the Commissioner to appoint one at the company’s cost and to issue a default assessment.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Same penalties as IR4, with the addition of default assessments under s 92 of the Tax Administration Act 1994, collection action against New Zealand assets, and liability for incorrect treaty relief claims.
